cases.purpose: Shows largest, medium, directory, and sparse file in descending allocated size.
cases.oracle: BashOS documented ncdu browser contract: initial descending allocation order, n/name, s/size, a/apparent, keyboard selection and directory navigation. GNU du/stat in setup independently verify the private file-size ordering and sparse allocation; no reference ncdu UI is assumed.
cases.comparison: The private PTY driver captures raw output, step events and terminal modes with bounded time/output; each fixed contract predicate and natural status is checked independently in both builds. Independent GNU du allocation/apparent values and stat size/block/device metadata are retained before the original inequalities are tested.
cases.setup_script:
/usr/bin/truncate -s 32768 tree/a_sparse
read -r a unused < <(/usr/bin/du -s -B1 tree/a_sparse)
read -r d unused < <(/usr/bin/du -s -B1 tree/adir)
read -r m unused < <(/usr/bin/du -s -B1 tree/mmedium)
read -r z unused < <(/usr/bin/du -s -B1 tree/zlarge)
printf 'a_sparse=%s\nadir=%s\nmmedium=%s\nzlarge=%s\n' "$a" "$d" "$m" "$z" > "$HOME/ncdu-allocation.txt"
/usr/bin/du -s --apparent-size -B1 tree/a_sparse tree/adir tree/mmedium tree/zlarge > "$HOME/ncdu-apparent.txt"
/usr/bin/stat -c '%n size=%s blocks=%b block_size=%B device=%d' tree/a_sparse tree/adir tree/mmedium tree/zlarge > "$HOME/ncdu-stat.txt"
(( a < d && d < m && m < z && z < 32768 ))
